newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian trade balance improves - bank.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian trade balance improves - bank.

text.p: Higher export earnings boosted Tanzania's trade balance in September, despite a slightly higher rate of inflation, the country's central bank reported on Sunday.
The Bank of Tanzania's monthly review said export earnings rose by 65 percent against the same month last year -- from $35.6 million to $58.7 million.

For the January-September period, the trade deficit was $496.6 million, against $732.1 million for the same period of 1995. Export earnings were 12.8 percent higher at $508.9 million against $451.2 million.

The latest estimate for annual inflation is 18.8 percent -- up by 0.8 percent over the past month. But the bank says it is not unduly worried by this "slight increase" brought about by higher fuel, power and water charges.
"The September rate of inflation represents an improvement of 7.7 percent compared with September 1995," the report added.
A senior bank official told Reuters he expected to see inflation down to 15 percent or lower by the end of the year.

The bank's report welcomes increased government efficiency in revenue collection, which amounted to 51.1 billion shillings ($85.47 million) for September. For the July-September quarter, government revenue represented 3.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Income tax collections during September were more than double those for August.
Yields on 90-day Treasury bills increased from 12.4 to 13.3 percent during September.
